definitionEn: a senior official appointed to lead a public body or oversee a particular area
situation: A senior official is appointed to run a public body or to protect people's rights in a particular area.

examples.text: The police [[commissioner]] promised to put more officers on the streets at night.
The children's [[commissioner]] has published a report on the mental health of teenagers.
The league [[commissioner]] suspended the player for three games after the incident.

texts: The new [[commissioner]] will investigate complaints about the police.
She was appointed information [[commissioner]] last year.
The [[commissioner]] refused to comment on the leaked report.

badCollocation.noteRu: Членов экзаменационной комиссии называют examiners. Commissioner — высокопоставленный чиновник, глава ведомства или член комиссии.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Назначить на должность — appoint (a commissioner, a director). Employ — брать на работу по найму, а put и set здесь вообще не подходят.

nuance.text: The [[commissioner]] herself will present the findings to parliament.
nuance.explanationRu: Commissioner — один человек, уполномоченный или глава ведомства. Commission — сама комиссия, то есть группа людей, поэтому herself к ней не подходит.

reverse.text: A special [[commission]] of ten experts will investigate the accident.
reverse.explanationRu: Группа экспертов — a commission. Commissioner — один человек, член или глава такой комиссии.

fixIt.text: The new police [[commissar]] has promised to cut street crime by half.
fixIt.explanationRu: Глава полиции — police commissioner. Commissar — политический комиссар в советской армии, в современном контексте так не говорят.

wordFormation.text: She was appointed as the first [[commissioner]] for older people.

definitionEn: a raw material or basic product, such as oil or wheat, that is bought and sold
senseNote: Здесь — товар или сырьё на рынке; в переносном смысле: time is a precious commodity — «время — ценный ресурс».
situation: Traders and economists talk about oil, gold, wheat, coffee or other goods sold in large amounts.

examples.text: Oil is the country's main export [[commodity]], so falling prices hit the economy hard.
Coffee is one of the most widely traded [[commodities]] in the world.
When [[commodity]] prices rise, the cost of bread and petrol soon follows.

texts: Gold is a [[commodity]] that investors buy in uncertain times.
Farmers follow the [[commodity]] markets closely before selling their wheat.
Sugar was once a luxury [[commodity]] that only the rich could afford.

badCollocation.noteRu: Товары в магазине — products или goods. Commodities — сырьё и базовые товары на рынке: нефть, зерно, металлы.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Цены на сырьё и базовые товары — commodity prices. Goods и wares в роли определения перед prices не используются, а stuff — разговорное «вещи».

nuance.text: Wheat is sold as a [[commodity]], so one farmer's crop is worth the same as another's.
nuance.explanationRu: Commodity — сырьё или базовый товар, где партии одинаковы и различаются только ценой: нефть, пшеница. Product — готовое изделие компании, часто со своим брендом.

reverse.text: The company is launching a new skincare [[product]] next month.
reverse.explanationRu: Новый крем бренда — product. Commodity — сырьё вроде нефти или зерна, а не изделие с брендом.

fixIt.text: Like oil, cocoa is a [[merchandise]] whose price changes every day on world markets.
fixIt.explanationRu: Биржевой товар вроде какао или нефти — commodity. Merchandise — товары в магазине или сувенирная продукция, и это слово неисчисляемое.

definitionEn: connected with a system in which the state owns and runs all land and industry
situation: You describe a party, state or historical period based on public ownership, such as Eastern Europe before 1990.

examples.text: My grandparents grew up in [[communist]] Poland and have many stories about life before 1989.
Under the [[communist]] system, the state owned every factory, farm and shop.
The city centre is full of grey concrete blocks built during the [[communist]] era.

texts: Several former [[communist]] countries joined the European Union in 2004.
He was a member of the [[communist]] youth organisation as a teenager.
The museum shows everyday objects from the [[communist]] period.

badCollocation.noteRu: Коммунальная квартира — a communal flat (или shared flat). Communist значит «коммунистический» и относится к политике и идеологии.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Эпоха коммунизма — the communist era. Communal — общий, коммунальный, community — сообщество, commune — коммуна.

nuance.text: China, Vietnam and Cuba all have [[communist]] governments.
nuance.explanationRu: Communist — о любой стране или партии с этой идеологией. Soviet относится только к СССР, а Китай, Вьетнам и Куба в него не входили.

reverse.text: My father did his military service in the [[Soviet]] army in the 1980s.
reverse.explanationRu: Армия СССР — the Soviet army. Для официальных названий, связанных с СССР, используют Soviet, а не communist.

fixIt.text: Many buildings from the [[communism]] period are now protected by law.
fixIt.explanationRu: Перед существительным period нужно прилагательное: the communist period. Communism — существительное, «коммунизм».

wordFormation.text: Life in the region changed dramatically after the collapse of [[communism]] in 1989.

definitionEn: a person or animal that you spend a lot of time with or travel with
senseNote: Здесь — тот, кто рядом и составляет компанию (a travelling companion, a constant companion); партнёра по бизнесу так не называют.
situation: Someone, often a friend, partner or pet, is by your side on a journey or through daily life.

examples.text: My [[companion]] on the long train journey was a retired teacher who told brilliant stories.
For many older people living alone, a dog is a loyal [[companion]] as well as a pet.
For years after the accident, pain was her constant [[companion]].

texts: He was the perfect travelling [[companion]]: calm, funny and never late.
The charity finds a volunteer [[companion]] for isolated elderly people.
Her diary became her closest [[companion]] during the long winter.

badCollocation.noteRu: Партнёр по бизнесу — a business partner. Companion — тот, кто составляет компанию: спутник, попутчик, друг.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Попутчик — a travelling companion (или travel companion). Journey, trip и road в этом сочетании не используются.

nuance.text: She hired a [[companion]] to live with her elderly mother.
nuance.explanationRu: Companion — человек, который находится рядом и составляет компанию. Company — общество, присутствие людей или фирма; hire a company значит «нанять фирму».

reverse.text: Thanks for coming — I really enjoyed your [[company]] this evening.
reverse.explanationRu: Приятно провести с кем-то время — enjoy someone's company. Companion — сам человек-спутник, а не общение с ним.

fixIt.text: My [[comrade]] on the long flight was a chatty nine-year-old boy.
fixIt.explanationRu: Попутчик, спутник — companion. Comrade — «товарищ» в политическом или военном смысле, о случайном попутчике так не говорят.

wordFormation.text: Many people get a pet for [[companionship]] rather than protection.

reply.context: A friend says: "I'm travelling around Portugal for a month, but I don't really want to go alone."
options: Why not post in that travel group? You might find a companion for part of the trip.
Take a companion — someone who'll stay at home and water your plants.
One may wish to procure a suitable companion via the appropriate channels.
reply.explanationRu: Companion — тот, кто едет или проводит время с тобой, а не остаётся дома. Третий вариант звучит чопорно и официально, другу так не советуют.

definitionEn: similar in size, amount or quality to something else
situation: You say that two salaries, prices, results or experiences are roughly the same, so they can be fairly judged side by side.

examples.text: Nurses here earn far less than workers in [[comparable]] jobs in the private sector.
The two groups were [[comparable]] in age, income and education, which made the results more reliable.
House prices in the town are [[comparable]] with those in the capital, which surprises most visitors.

texts: Salaries here are [[comparable]] to those in London.
We have no [[comparable]] data from before 2010.
Nothing I've tasted is [[comparable]] to my grandmother's apple pie.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Сравнимый по размеру, цене» — comparable in size, in price; предлог by здесь не используется.

collocationTask.explanationRu: После comparable ставят to или with: comparable with those in the capital. As, than и for здесь не используются.

nuance.text: The two cities have [[comparable]] populations of around two million.
nuance.explanationRu: Comparable — сопоставимый, примерно такой же по размеру или качеству. Comparative — сравнительный, основанный на сравнении: a comparative study.

reverse.text: She wrote a [[comparative]] study of education in Finland and Japan.
reverse.explanationRu: Исследование, которое сравнивает две системы, — a comparative study. Comparable значит «сопоставимый, похожий».

fixIt.text: Rents here are [[compatible]] with those in the city centre, so why not live closer to work?
fixIt.explanationRu: Сопоставимый по уровню — comparable. Compatible — совместимый (о технике или людях): compatible software, compatible personalities.

wordFormation.text: The two schools are [[comparable]] in size but get very different results.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Is the new job better paid than your old one?"
options: Yes, the salary is comparable — it's almost twice as much!
Not really — the salary is comparable, but the hours are much better.
The remuneration is comparable, as per my contractual documentation.
reply.explanationRu: Comparable — примерно такой же, поэтому «сопоставимая зарплата, почти вдвое больше» — противоречие. Третий ответ звучит как отчёт, а не разговор с другом.

rewrite.original: A flat here costs about the same as a flat in the capital.
rewrite.frame: The price of a flat here is ____ the price in the capital.
rewrite.explanationRu: Примерно такой же по уровню — comparable to (with).

definitionEn: caring concern for someone who is suffering, together with a wish to help them
situation: You see a person or animal in pain or trouble and feel a strong wish to help them.

examples.text: The nurses treated my grandmother with such [[compassion]] in her final weeks that we sent them flowers afterwards.
The judge showed [[compassion]] and gave the young mother a suspended sentence instead of prison.
Instead of criticising yourself for every mistake, try to treat yourself with the same [[compassion]] you'd show a friend.

texts: She became a doctor out of [[compassion]], not for the money.
The film asks us to feel [[compassion]] even for the villain.
His letter to the grieving family was full of [[compassion]].

badCollocation.noteRu: Сострадание к кому-то — compassion for someone: нужен предлог for, а не to.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Проявить сострадание — show compassion (или feel compassion for). Make, do и put с compassion не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Good doctors combine medical skill with genuine [[compassion]] for their patients.
nuance.explanationRu: Compassion — сострадание с уважением и желанием помочь. Pity — жалость, часто сверху вниз; хорошему врачу нужна compassion, а не pity.

reverse.text: I don't need your [[pity]] — I need a job.
reverse.explanationRu: Отвергая жалость к себе, говорят I don't need your pity. Compassion — тёплое, уважительное чувство, от него так резко не отказываются.

fixIt.text: The nurse showed great [[condolence]] to every patient on the ward.
fixIt.explanationRu: Condolences — соболезнования по поводу чьей-то смерти (my condolences). Сострадание к больным — compassion.

wordFormation.text: She is a kind and [[compassionate]] manager who always listens.

reply.context: A colleague tells you: "I've been so stressed since my dad got ill. I keep making mistakes at work."
options: I'm so sorry. Show some compassion to yourself and just work harder, then.
Your situation elicits my compassion. Please proceed with your tasks.
I'm so sorry. Try to show yourself some compassion — anyone would struggle right now.
reply.explanationRu: Compassion — сочувствие и бережность, а не требование работать усерднее. Второй ответ звучит холодно и официально.

definitionEn: to force someone to do something, especially by law, duty or strong feeling
situation: A law, a rule, a situation or a strong inner feeling forces someone to act, even if they don't want to.

examples.text: The new law will [[compel]] landlords to fix serious problems within fourteen days.
I felt [[compelled]] to say something when my colleague took credit for my work.
Heavy snow [[compelled]] the airport to cancel all flights for the second day running.

texts: Staff were [[compelled]] to work overtime during the busy season.
She felt [[compelled]] to apologise, even though it wasn't her fault.
Nobody can be [[compelled]] to give evidence against their own family.

badCollocation.noteRu: После compel нужно to: compel someone to do something. Без to употребляется только make: make someone do.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Чувствовать, что должен что-то сделать, — feel compelled to. Compelling — «убедительный», compulsory — «обязательный», complied — от comply «подчиниться».

nuance.text: The court can [[compel]] a witness to attend if they refuse to come voluntarily.
nuance.explanationRu: Compel — принудить, в том числе по закону: суд может заставить свидетеля явиться. Persuade — убедить словами, а у суда здесь есть власть, а не только аргументы.

reverse.text: My sister [[persuaded]] me to try yoga, and now I love it.
reverse.explanationRu: Уговорить, убедить — persuade. Compel — принудить силой или законом, для дружеского совета это слишком жёстко.

fixIt.text: The court [[pushed]] the company to refund every customer who had been overcharged.
fixIt.explanationRu: Суд принуждает по закону — compel (или order). Push — «подталкивать, давить», разговорное слово, для решения суда не подходит.

wordFormation.text: Wearing a helmet is [[compulsory]] for all cyclists in the race.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Why did you give that street musician twenty euros?"
options: He compelled me to take a photo of him — he said it was fine.
He was so good that I felt compelled to. I've never heard the violin played like that.
I was compelled by the aesthetic merit of the performance to make a remittance.
reply.explanationRu: Compel — принуждать, а не разрешать. Третий ответ звучит как казённый отчёт, а не разговор с другом.

rewrite.original: The new rules force all drivers to take a test every ten years.
rewrite.frame: Under the new rules, all drivers ____ take a test every ten years.
rewrite.explanationRu: Пассив: drivers are compelled to do something.

definitionEn: so strong or convincing that you have to accept or believe it
senseNote: Здесь — «убедительный» (compelling evidence); о книге или фильме compelling значит «захватывающий» (a compelling read).
situation: An argument, a reason or a piece of evidence is so strong that people find it hard to disagree.

examples.text: The police found [[compelling]] evidence that the fire had been started deliberately.
She made such a [[compelling]] case for a four-day week that the board agreed immediately.
Honestly, I can't think of a single [[compelling]] reason to buy the new model.

texts: The lawyer presented a [[compelling]] argument for her client's innocence.
There is [[compelling]] evidence that sleep affects memory.
We need a [[compelling]] reason to change a system that works.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Убедительная просьба» в объявлениях — please или we strongly ask you. Compelling описывает доводы и доказательства, а не просьбы.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Убедительно обосновать что-то — make a compelling case for something. Story, reason и fact с make в этом выражении не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Scientists now have [[compelling]] evidence that the drug works.
nuance.explanationRu: Compelling — убедительный, такой, с которым трудно спорить. Compulsory — обязательный по правилам: compulsory education, compulsory military service.

reverse.text: Physical education is [[compulsory]] for all students until the age of sixteen.
reverse.explanationRu: Обязательный по правилам — compulsory. Compelling значит «убедительный» и к школьным предметам не подходит.

fixIt.text: The prosecution failed to present any [[convinced]] evidence against him.
fixIt.explanationRu: Convinced — «убеждённый», о человеке. Доказательства, которые убеждают, — compelling (или convincing) evidence.

wordFormation.text: The report makes a [[compelling]] argument for investing in public transport.

reply.context: Your manager asks: "Why should we hire this candidate rather than the other one?"
options: Her portfolio is, like, well compelling, innit.
Her portfolio is compelling — it's quite weak and unconvincing, actually.
Her portfolio is really compelling. Every project shows exactly the skills we need.
reply.explanationRu: Compelling — убедительный и сильный, поэтому «убедительное, но слабое» — противоречие. Первый ответ — сленг, с руководителем так не говорят.

rewrite.original: It's hard to argue with the evidence that the drug works.
rewrite.frame: There is ____ that the drug works.
rewrite.explanationRu: Доказательства, с которыми трудно спорить, — compelling evidence.

definitionEn: to balance a weakness, loss or problem with something good that reduces its effect
senseNote: Здесь — «восполнять недостаток» (compensate for); о выплате денег пострадавшим — compensate someone for damage.
situation: Something good, such as effort or a special feature, makes up for a weakness, a loss or a disadvantage.

examples.text: What she lacks in experience, she more than [[compensates]] for with energy and curiosity.
When one ear is damaged, the brain learns to [[compensate]] by relying more on the other.
The flat is tiny, but huge windows and pale walls [[compensate]] for the lack of space.

texts: Nothing can [[compensate]] for the loss of a parent.
Good lighting can [[compensate]] for a small, dark kitchen.
Some people talk loudly to [[compensate]] for feeling insecure.

badCollocation.noteRu: Восполнить недостаток — compensate for something, с предлогом for. Без for compensate значит «выплатить компенсацию кому-то».

collocationTask.prompt: more than ___ for his lack of height
collocationTask.explanationRu: С лихвой восполнить недостаток — more than compensate for (или make up for). Cover, answer и replace в этой конструкции не используются.

nuance.text: His hard work [[compensates]] for his lack of natural talent.
nuance.explanationRu: Compensate for — восполнять недостаток: трудолюбие перекрывает нехватку таланта. Complement — удачно дополнять что-то хорошее: the wine complements the fish.

reverse.text: A crisp white wine [[complements]] the fish perfectly.
reverse.explanationRu: Удачно дополнять — complement: вино подчёркивает вкус рыбы. Compensate for — восполнять недостаток, а с рыбой всё в порядке.

fixIt.text: Heavy rain in spring can [[replace]] for a dry winter, so farmers are hopeful.
fixIt.explanationRu: Восполнять недостаток — compensate for something. Replace — заменять одно другим, и предлог for после него не ставят.

wordFormation.text: Many people eat sweets as a kind of [[compensation]] for stress.

reply.context: A friend shows you around a flat and says: "It's a bit far from the centre, but look at that view!"
options: True, the view compensates for it — it makes the commute even longer.
The panorama compensates for the distance, as per my assessment.
Honestly, a view like that more than compensates for a longer commute.
reply.explanationRu: Compensate for — перевешивать минус чем-то хорошим, а не делать хуже. Второй ответ звучит как отчёт оценщика, а не реплика другу.

rewrite.original: His charm makes up for his lack of experience.
rewrite.frame: His charm ____ his lack of experience.
rewrite.explanationRu: Make up for и compensate for здесь синонимы: «восполнять».

definitionEn: money paid to someone because they have suffered injury, loss or damage
senseNote: Здесь — денежная компенсация; также compensation — «утешение, плюс» (getting older has its compensations), а в США — зарплата с бонусами.
situation: A company, airline or court pays money to someone who has been hurt, delayed or has lost property.

examples.text: Passengers whose flights are delayed by more than three hours may be entitled to [[compensation]].
After the accident at the factory, she received [[compensation]] for her injuries.
The court ordered the company to pay £50,000 in [[compensation]] to the families.

texts: The airline offered us [[compensation]] for the lost luggage.
Victims of the fraud will receive full [[compensation]].
He is suing his employer for [[compensation]] after a fall at work.

badCollocation.noteRu: В значении «денежное возмещение» compensation — неисчисляемое: pay compensation, без артикля a.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Требовать компенсацию — claim compensation. Ask требует for (ask for compensation), а take и earn с compensation в этом смысле не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The airline returned the ticket price and also paid [[compensation]] for the ruined holiday.
nuance.explanationRu: Refund — возврат уплаченных денег. Compensation — деньги сверх этого за причинённый ущерб или неудобства, как за испорченный отпуск.

reverse.text: The shoes fell apart after a week, so I asked for a [[refund]].
reverse.explanationRu: Вернуть деньги за бракованную покупку — ask for a refund. Compensation — возмещение ущерба, а не возврат цены товара.

fixIt.text: The airline paid every passenger €250 in [[penalty]] for the cancelled flight.
fixIt.explanationRu: Деньги, которые получает пострадавший пассажир, — compensation. Penalty — штраф, который платят в наказание, обычно государству или по договору.

wordFormation.text: The insurance company refused to [[compensate]] us for the storm damage.

reply.context: A friend texts: "The airline lost my suitcase, and I've spent 300 euros on new clothes!"
options: Keep all the receipts and claim compensation — they have to pay you back.
Ask them for compensation — a nice card saying sorry should be enough.
One is advised to lodge a formal compensation claim forthwith.
reply.explanationRu: Compensation — денежное возмещение ущерба, а не открытка с извинениями. Третий ответ звучит как юрист в суде, а не как совет другу.

rewrite.original: The company paid the workers money for their injuries.
rewrite.frame: The workers received ____ for their injuries.
rewrite.explanationRu: Деньги за травму или ущерб — compensation.
